# Purplefish Agent

[![Test](https://github.com/purplefish-ai/agent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/purplefish-ai/agent/actions/workflows/test.yml)

This is our livekit based phone agent.

## Development

### Setup

1. Install the 1Password CLI: https://developer.1password.com/docs/cli/get-started/
2. Install uv: `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`
3. Install dependencies: `uv sync`
4. Install git hooks:
   ```bash
   # Install pre-commit hooks (runs on commit)
   pre-commit install

   # Install pre-push hooks (runs simulation tests on push)
   pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push

   # Or install both at once
   pre-commit install && pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push
   ```
5. Create local dev keys in Livekit
   1. Login to livekit, enter the `Local Dev <Your Name>` project (Martin will create this for you)
   2. go into Settings > Keys
   3. Create 1 new API Key
   4. Update the .env file to set the new API keys and Secrets. For local dev, we can use the same API key for all of these secrets.
      1. Set the API key to the values LIVEKIT_API_KEY_INBOUND, LIVEKIT_API_KEY_OUTBOUND
      2. Set the secret key to the values LIVEKIT_API_SECRET_INBOUND, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET_OUTBOUND
      3. Set the Websocket URL to the values LIVEKIT_URL_INBOUND, LIVEKIT_URL_OUTBOUND
6. Download the model files for livekit `make download-files`
7. Run the agent: `make dev`

## Testing the agent locally using the livekit playground
1. Find the profile you wish to test and copy the profile id
2. Paste the profile id into the default value for the `PLAYGROUND_PROFILE_ID` env var in `env.ts` on the *MONOREPO* (not in the agent repo)
3. Connect to the livekit agent playground by visiting this URL: https://agents-playground.livekit.io/
4. Select your local dev env
5. This will launch a new interview locally.

## Testing Tools

### Simulation Mode
Simulation mode allows you to run automated conversations between the agent and an AI-powered candidate using real job IDs.

**Usage:**
```bash
# Basic simulation
make simulate <job_id>

# With custom parameters
make simulate <job_id> max_turns=30
make simulate <job_id> instructions="You are an experienced candidate"
```

The simulation will:
- Fetch real job and profile data from your development server
- Run an automated conversation with an AI candidate (GPT-4)
- Display color-coded conversation transcript
- Provide evaluation of interview completion

### Interactive Chat Mode
Chat mode lets you interact directly with the agent as a candidate through text input.

**Usage:**
```bash
# Start interactive chat
make chat <job_id>
```

Features:
- Real-time text interaction with the agent
- You play the role of the candidate
- No turn limits - chat as long as you want
- Type 'exit', 'quit', 'bye', or 'goodbye' to end
- Color-coded output (your messages in green, agent in cyan)

Both modes create a room name in format `demo:{job_id}_{unique_id}` and use the real job data from your system.

## Debugging
If you need to run the agent through your IDE so that you can debug, here's how to do it
- Entrypoint should be the `agent` script. The agent script will be in your uv virtual environment at `.venv/bin/agent`
- Run the script with the param `start`
- You might need to configure your IDE to write secrets to a file before you launch. Here's an example command you can use for that: `inject -f -i ./envs/.env -o ./envs/local`

## Running lints and checks locally

### Pre-commit hooks
After making changes locally, you can manually run the hooks:
```bash
# Run all pre-commit hooks on all files
pre-commit run --all-files

# Run specific hook
pre-commit run ty --all-files
pre-commit run ruff-check --all-files

# Run ty type checker directly (10-20x faster than mypy/pyright)
make ty-check
# Note: ty is in pre-alpha stage, expect some false positives
```

### Pre-push hooks
To manually run pre-push checks:
```bash
# Run simulation tests (same as what happens on git push)
make run-simulation

# Or run pre-push hooks manually
pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push
```

This will let you catch lint issues and test failures before committing/pushing.

## Running the LiveKit CLI

We have a wrapper around the LiveKit CLI that respects the .env file.

First, install the LiveKit CLI with `brew install livekit-cli`

Run the LiveKit CLI with `uv run livekit <args...>`

## Testing

The project separates unit tests from simulation tests for better organization and faster CI/CD.

### Unit Tests

To run unit tests (excluding simulation tests):
```bash
# Run all unit tests in parallel
make test

# Run a specific test file or test
make test path=tests/unit/test_example.py
make test path=tests/unit/test_example.py::test_specific_function
```

Unit tests are run in parallel using pytest-xdist for faster execution and automatically exclude any simulation test directories.

### Simulation Tests

To run simulation tests (integration tests that simulate full conversations):
```bash
# Run all simulation tests
make run-simulation
```

Simulation tests:
- Run with retry logic (3 attempts with 1 second delay)
- Stop on first failure for easier debugging
- Test end-to-end agent behavior with simulated conversations
- **Note**: Simulation tests run automatically during `git push` via pre-push hook. To bypass this check, use `git push --no-verify`

### Code Coverage

We use pytest-cov to track code coverage. Coverage reports are automatically generated in CI/CD for all PRs.

**Running tests with coverage locally:**
```bash
# Run all tests with coverage
make test-cov

# Run specific test with coverage
make test-cov path=tests/unit/test_example.py

# Check coverage summary
uv run python scripts/check_coverage.py
```

**Coverage outputs:**
- **Terminal**: Coverage summary shown after tests complete
- **HTML Report**: Open `htmlcov/index.html` in your browser for detailed line-by-line coverage
- **XML Report**: `coverage.xml` for CI/CD integration

**Coverage in Pull Requests:**
- Coverage reports are automatically posted as PR comments (free, no external service required)
- Lines missing coverage are annotated in the PR diff
- Visual indicators: 🟢 85%+ | 🟡 70-84% | 🔴 <70%
- Coverage summary available in GitHub Actions job summary
- HTML coverage reports uploaded as artifacts for detailed analysis

**Current coverage targets:**
- Overall project: 70% minimum (aiming for 80%+)
- New code in PRs: 80% minimum

To get a more end-to-end-test, run purplefish-ai/app with inngest (`npm run inngest`). After the call, from the app
folder, run `npm run send-end-of-room-event` to trigger all of the end of room logic, including sending emails and SMS.

## Voice Agent v4

Voice Agent v4 introduces a new architecture with modular task-based agents. The foundation includes:
- **Task Orchestrator**: Manages conversation flow through defined tasks
- **Specialized Agents**: Greeter, DataCollection, Information, and Closer agents for different conversation phases
- **Dynamic Tool Factory**: Creates conversation tools based on script configuration
- **Conversation Context**: Maintains state and data points throughout the call
- **Script-Driven Architecture**: JSON-based call scripts define agent behavior and conversation flow

### Running Voice Agent v4 Locally

To test the new Voice Agent v4 with the local development command:

```bash
# Run with 1Password for environment variables and uv
op run --env-file=".voice_agent.env.example" -- uv run voice_agent_local_dev --call-script-path examples/it_support_call_script.json
```

For all local_dev options run
```bash
op run --env-file=".voice_agent.env.example" -- uv run voice_agent_local_dev --help
```

This command:
- Uses 1Password CLI to load environment variables from `.voice_agent.env.example`
- Runs the voice agent v4 local development mode
- Loads the example IT support call script for testing

## Docker Build and Run Guide

This guide explains how to build and run the Purplefish AI voice agent Docker image locally.

### Prerequisites

- Docker installed on your system
- 1Password CLI configured (for production deployment)
- Environment variables configured

### Building the Docker Image

Build the Docker image with:

```bash
docker build -t purplefish-agent:latest .
```

For a specific Python version:

```bash
docker build --build-arg PYTHON_VERSION=3.11 -t purplefish-agent:latest .
```

### Running the Docker Container

#### Development Mode (Local Testing)

For local development without 1Password integration, run with environment variables. See `envs/production.env` for the required variables:

```bash
# Set environment to bypass 1Password injection
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  -e VARIABLE_NAME="value" \
  # ... add all variables from envs/production.env ... \
  # can also pass in --env-file ./.env \
  purplefish-agent:latest
```

#### Production Mode (with 1Password)

For production deployment with 1Password service account:

```bash
docker run -it --rm \
  -e OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN="your-1password-service-account-token" \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Production \
  purplefish-agent:latest
```

#### Docker Command

By default, the container runs with `agent start` command

To run a different command (clarify in pyproject.toml project.scripts)

```bash
# Generate development room token
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  # ... environment variables from envs/production.env ... \
  purplefish-agent:latest voice_agent_local_dev --call-script-path "..." --no-simulate-room

# Generate development room token
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  # ... environment variables from envs/production.env ... \
  purplefish-agent:latest generate_dev_room_token

# download livekit plugin
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  # ... environment variables from envs/production.env ... \
  purplefish-agent:latest download_livekit_plugin_model
```

### Environment Variables

The container requires environment variables defined in `envs/production.env`. When running locally without 1Password:

- Set `AGENT_ENV=Development` to bypass 1Password injection
- Provide actual values for all variables listed in `envs/production.env`

For production with 1Password:
- Set `AGENT_ENV=Production`
- Provide `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` for 1Password service account access

### How It Works

1. The Dockerfile creates a lightweight Python 3.11 image
2. Installs system dependencies and required tools (1Password CLI, uv)
3. Creates a non-root user for security
4. Installs Python dependencies and downloads LiveKit plugin models
5. Uses `docker_entrypoint.sh` to handle environment setup:
   - In Production mode: Injects secrets from 1Password
   - In other modes: Uses passed environment variables
6. Runs the agent with DataDog tracing enabled

### Troubleshooting

- **Missing environment variables**: Ensure all required variables are set when not using 1Password
- **1Password errors**: Verify your service account token is valid and has access to required secrets
- **Model download issues**: The container pre-downloads LiveKit plugin models during build
- **Permission errors**: The container runs as non-root user `appuser` for security

## Versioning and Releases

This project uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) and [python-semantic-release](https://python-semantic-release.readthedocs.io/) for version management.

### Commit Message Convention
We follow the [Conventional Commits specification](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):

- `feat:` New feature (minor version bump)
- `fix:` Bug fix (patch version bump)
- `docs:` Documentation changes (no version bump)
- `style:` Code style changes (no version bump)
- `refactor:` Code refactoring (no version bump)
- `perf:` Performance improvements (patch version bump)
- `test:` Test changes (no version bump)
- `chore:` Build process or auxiliary tool changes (no version bump)
- `BREAKING CHANGE:` or `!` after type (major version bump)

Examples:
```
feat: add voice agent v4 support
fix: resolve timeout issue in call controller
feat!: redesign agent manager API
```

### Manual Release Process

To create a new release:

```bash
# Check what version will be released (dry run)
uv run semantic-release version --print

# Create a new version (updates version in pyproject.toml, creates git tag, updates CHANGELOG.md)
uv run semantic-release version

# Push the changes and tags to trigger GitHub release
git push --follow-tags origin main

# Optionally publish to GitHub releases
uv run semantic-release publish
```

The release process will:
1. Analyze commits since last release
2. Determine version bump based on commit types
3. Update version in `pyproject.toml`
4. Generate/update `CHANGELOG.md`
5. Create git tag with version
6. Create GitHub release with changelog

import asyncio
import sys
import threading
import traceback
import types
from typing import Any
from typing import Callable
from typing import Optional
from typing import Tuple

from livekit.agents import AutoSubscribe
from livekit.agents import JobContext
from livekit.agents.llm import LLM

from agent.agents.llm_model import load_llm_model
from agent.agents.pronunciation_filter import PronunciationFilter
from agent.call_controller import CallController
from agent.log import logger
from agent.schemas.profile_v1 import Job
from agent.schemas.profile_v1 import Organization
from agent.schemas.profile_v1 import Profile
from agent.services.container import ServiceContainer
from agent.services.impl.livekit_service import LiveKitService
from agent.services.impl.purplefish_service import PurplefishService
from agent.services.interfaces.purplefish_service import Engagement


def dump_all_stacks(ctx: JobContext) -> None:
    logger.info(
        "=== STACK DUMP ===",
        extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
    )
    for thread_id, frame in sys._current_frames().items():
        logger.info(
            f"--- Thread {thread_id} ({threading.current_thread().name}) ---",
            extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
        )
        for line in traceback.format_stack(frame):
            logger.info(
                line.rstrip(),
                extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
            )
    # log outstanding asyncio tasks
    logger.info(
        "=== OUTSTANDING TASKS ===",
        extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
    )
    for task in asyncio.all_tasks():
        # Get the coroutine's current frame if available
        coro = task.get_coro()
        cr_frame: types.FrameType | None = None
        if coro is not None and hasattr(coro, "cr_frame"):
            cr_frame = coro.cr_frame

        # Get method name if frame exists
        method = cr_frame.f_code.co_name if cr_frame is not None else "unknown"

        logger.info(
            f"Task {task.get_name()}: status={task._state} done={task.done()} waiting_in={method}",
            extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
        )
    logger.info(
        "=== END STACK DUMP ===",
        extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
    )


def create_exception_handler(
    ctx: JobContext,
) -> Callable[[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, dict[str, Any]], None]:
    def handle_asyncio_exception(
        loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, context: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        msg = context.get("message", "")
        exc = context.get("exception", None)

        logger.error(
            f"Asyncio uncaught exception: {msg}",
            exc_info=exc,
            extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
        )

    return handle_asyncio_exception


async def setup_connection(ctx: JobContext, services: ServiceContainer) -> None:
    """Set up the connection to the room and configure exception handling."""
    asyncio.get_event_loop().set_exception_handler(create_exception_handler(ctx))

    logger.info(
        "Connecting to room",
        extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
    )

    ctx.add_shutdown_callback(lambda: services.livekit.hangup(ctx))
    await ctx.connect(auto_subscribe=AutoSubscribe.AUDIO_ONLY)

    logger.info(
        "Connected to room",
        extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
    )


async def fetch_and_validate_candidate_data(
    ctx: JobContext, services: ServiceContainer
) -> Optional[Any]:
    """Fetch candidate profile and validate the data."""
    logger.info(
        "Fetching candidate profile",
        extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
    )

    candidate_data = await services.purplefish.get_candidate_profile(ctx)

    if not candidate_data:
        logger.warning(
            "Failed to get candidate profile and job details",
            extra={
                "job_id": ctx.job.id,
                "room_name": ctx.job.room.name,
                "error": "No candidate data returned from API",
            },
        )
        logger.info(
            "Initiating shutdown - no candidate data",
            extra={
                "job_id": ctx.job.id,
                "room_name": ctx.job.room.name,
                "shutdown_reason": "Failed to get candidate profile and job details",
            },
        )
        ctx.shutdown("Failed to get candidate profile and job details")
        return None

    # Log job data returned by purplefish
    logger.info(
        f"Loaded job data: {candidate_data.job.id}",
        extra={
            "job_id": ctx.job.id,
            "room_name": ctx.job.room.name,
            "closer": candidate_data.job.closer,
        },
    )

    if candidate_data.job.scriptNodes is None:
        raise Exception("Failed to get script nodes")

    return candidate_data


async def create_and_validate_engagement(
    ctx: JobContext,
    services: ServiceContainer,
    candidate_profile: Profile,
) -> Optional[Engagement]:
    """Create engagement and validate it's newly created."""
    engagement = await services.purplefish.create_engagement(ctx, candidate_profile)

    logger.info(
        f"Created engagement {engagement.id}",
        extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
    )

    if not engagement.isNewlyCreated:
        logger.warning(
            "Engagement has already been created/handled. Aborting.",
            extra={
                "job_id": ctx.job.id,
                "room_name": ctx.job.room.name,
                "engagement_id": engagement.id,
                "isNewlyCreated": engagement.isNewlyCreated,
            },
        )
        dump_all_stacks(ctx)
        logger.info(
            "Initiating shutdown - engagement already exists",
            extra={
                "job_id": ctx.job.id,
                "room_name": ctx.job.room.name,
                "shutdown_reason": "Engagement has already been created/handled (it likely froze - see logs).",
            },
        )
        ctx.shutdown(
            "Engagement has already been created/handled (it likely froze - see logs)."
        )
        return None

    return engagement


async def load_and_update_engagement_components(
    ctx: JobContext,
    services: ServiceContainer,
    organization: Organization,
    job: Job,
    candidate_profile: Profile,
    engagement: Engagement,
) -> Tuple[LLM[Any], str]:
    """Load AI components and update engagement with model information."""
    # Preload components
    llm_model, model_name = await load_llm_model(ctx, organization)

    try:
        await services.purplefish.update_engagement(
            engagement_id=engagement.id,
            agentModel=model_name,
            livekitJobId=ctx.job.id,
        )
        logger.info(
            "Updated engagement with agent model and job ID",
            extra={
                "job_id": ctx.job.id,
                "room_name": ctx.job.room.name,
                "model_name": model_name,
                "engagement_id": engagement.id,
            },
        )
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(
            "Failed to update engagement with agent model",
            extra={
                "error": str(e),
                "job_id": ctx.job.id,
                "room_name": ctx.job.room.name,
                "model_name": model_name,
            },
        )

    return llm_model, model_name


async def load_pronunciation_filter(
    ctx: JobContext, services: ServiceContainer, organization: Organization
) -> Optional[PronunciationFilter]:
    """Load pronunciation filter from the Purplefish service."""
    try:
        pronunciation_dict = await services.purplefish.get_pronunciation_dictionary(
            organization.id
        )
        pronunciation_filter = PronunciationFilter(pronunciation_dict.entries)
        logger.info(
            f"Loaded pronunciation filter with {len(pronunciation_dict.entries)} entries for organization {organization.id}",
            extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
        )
        return pronunciation_filter
    except Exception:
        logger.warning(
            f"Failed to load pronunciation dictionary for organization {organization.id}",
            extra={"job_id": ctx.job.id, "room_name": ctx.job.room.name},
            exc_info=True,
        )
        return None


def create_call_controller(
    ctx: JobContext,
    services: ServiceContainer,
    llm_model: LLM[Any],
    organization: Organization,
    job: Job,
    candidate_profile: Profile,
    engagement: Engagement,
    pronunciation_filter: Optional[PronunciationFilter] = None,
) -> CallController:
    """Create and configure the CallController."""
    return CallController(
        ctx=ctx,
        llm_model=llm_model,
        organization=organization,
        job=job,
        profile=candidate_profile,
        engagement=Engagement(
            id=engagement.id,
            createdAt=engagement.createdAt,
            updatedAt=engagement.updatedAt,
            profileId=engagement.profileId,
            roomName=engagement.roomName,
            agentPhoneNumber=engagement.agentPhoneNumber,
            isNewlyCreated=engagement.isNewlyCreated,
        ),
        services=services,
        pronunciation_filter=pronunciation_filter,
    )


async def handle_outbound_call(
    ctx: JobContext,
    services: ServiceContainer,
    call_controller: CallController,
    engagement: Engagement,
    candidate_phone_number: str,
) -> bool:
    """Handle outbound call setup and connection."""
    assert engagement.agentPhoneNumber is not None
    assert engagement.agentPhoneNumber.sipOutboundTrunkId is not None

    await call_controller.start()

    sip_participant = await services.livekit.create_sip_participant_and_wait_for_pickup(
        ctx=ctx,
        outbound_trunk_id=engagement.agentPhoneNumber.sipOutboundTrunkId,
        number=candidate_phone_number,
        participant_name="Candidate",
    )

    if sip_participant is None:
        logger.info(
            "Initiating shutdown - outbound call not answered",
            extra={
                "job_id": ctx.job.id,
                "room_name": ctx.job.room.name,
                "candidate_phone": candidate_phone_number,
                "shutdown_reason": "Call not picked up",
            },
        )
        ctx.shutdown("Call not picked up")
        return False

    await call_controller.start_egress()
    return True


async def handle_inbound_call(call_controller: CallController) -> None:
    """Handle inbound call setup."""
    await call_controller.start()
    await call_controller.start_egress()


async def entrypoint_no_catch(ctx: JobContext, services: ServiceContainer) -> None:
    """Main entrypoint logic without exception handling."""
    # Set up connection
    await setup_connection(ctx, services)

    # Fetch and validate candidate data
    candidate_data = await fetch_and_validate_candidate_data(ctx, services)
    if not candidate_data:
        return

    # Extract data components
    candidate_profile = candidate_data.profile
    organization = candidate_data.organization
    job = candidate_data.job

    # Create and validate engagement
    engagement = await create_and_validate_engagement(ctx, services, candidate_profile)
    if not engagement:
        return

    # Load components and update engagement
    llm_model, model_name = await load_and_update_engagement_components(
        ctx, services, organization, job, candidate_profile, engagement
    )

    # Load pronunciation filter once for all agents
    pronunciation_filter = await load_pronunciation_filter(ctx, services, organization)

    # Create agent
    call_controller = create_call_controller(
        ctx=ctx,
        services=services,
        llm_model=llm_model,
        organization=organization,
        job=job,
        candidate_profile=candidate_profile,
        engagement=engagement,
        pronunciation_filter=pronunciation_filter,
    )

    # Handle call based on type
    if engagement.is_outbound_call():
        success = await handle_outbound_call(
            ctx, services, call_controller, engagement, candidate_profile.phoneNumber
        )
        if not success:
            return
    else:
        await handle_inbound_call(call_controller)


async def entrypoint(ctx: JobContext) -> None:
    """Main entrypoint with exception handling."""
    services = ServiceContainer(
        livekit_service=LiveKitService(),
        purplefish_service=PurplefishService(),
    )
    try:
        await entrypoint_no_catch(ctx, services)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception(
            "An error occurred in the agent entrypoint_fnc",
            extra={
                "job_id": ctx.job.id,
                "room_name": ctx.job.room.name,
                "exception_type": type(e).__name__,
                "exception_message": str(e),
            },
        )
        logger.info(
            "Initiating shutdown - unhandled exception",
            extra={
                "job_id": ctx.job.id,
                "room_name": ctx.job.room.name,
                "shutdown_reason": str(e),
            },
        )
        ctx.shutdown(str(e))

.PHONY: dev test test-cov download-files simulate chat replay

# Development environment
dev:
	op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run agent start

# Test environment
# Usage: make test          # Run all tests (excluding simulation directories)
# Usage: make test path=... # Run specific test file
test:
	@if [ -n "$(path)" ]; then \
		op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run pytest -vvvv -s $(path); \
	else \
	    op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run pytest -n auto -v -s --ignore-glob="**/simulation*"; \
	fi

# Run simulation tests only
# Usage: make simulation    # Run all simulation tests
run-simulation:
	op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run pytest -n auto -v -s tests/ -k "simulation" --maxfail=1 --tb=short --reruns=3 --reruns-delay=1

# Test with coverage report

test-cov:

	@if [ -n "$(path)" ]; then \
		op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run pytest -vvvv -s $(path) --cov=agent --cov=voice_agent --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html --cov-report=xml; \
	else \

	@echo "Coverage report generated:"

# Development environment
dev:
	op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run agent start

# Test environment
# Usage: make test          # Run all tests (excluding simulation directories)
# Usage: make test path=... # Run specific test file
test:
	@if [ -n "$(path)" ]; then \
		op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run pytest -vvvv -s $(path); \
	else \
	    op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run pytest -n auto -v -s --ignore-glob="**/simulation*"; \
	fi

	op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run pytest -n auto -v -s tests/ -k "simulation" --maxfail=1 --tb=short --reruns=3 --reruns-delay=1

# Test with coverage report
# Usage: make test-cov          # Run all tests with coverage

	else \

	fi
	@echo "Coverage report generated:"

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

This is the Purplefish AI voice agent - a LiveKit-based phone agent for conducting automated voice interviews. The agent uses WebRTC for real-time communication, Deepgram for speech-to-text, and various TTS providers (Cartesia, Google).

## Essential Commands

We have a `Makefile` that simplifies common tasks. Here are the key commands:

### Development
- `make dev` - Run the agent in development mode
- `make test` - Run all unit tests (excludes simulation tests, runs in parallel)
- `make test path=tests/path/to/test.py::test_name` - Run specific test
- `make run-simulation` - Run all simulation/integration tests (with retry logic)
- `make download-files` - Download required model files (run after initial setup)

### Code Quality
- `make check` - Run all linting and formatting checks (includes both ty and pyright)
- `make ty-check` - Run ty type checker (fast, Rust-based)
- `make pyright` - Run pyright type checker (comprehensive)
- uv manages dependencies - use `uv add` for new packages
- **Dual Type Checking System**:
  - **ty**: Astral's extremely fast Rust-based type checker (10-20x faster)
    - Run: `uv run ty check` or `make ty-check`
    - Pre-alpha stage with some false positives configured to be ignored
    - Best for quick feedback during development
  - **pyright**: Microsoft's comprehensive type checker
    - Run: `uv run pyright` or `make pyright`
    - More mature and accurate, better for CI/CD
    - Configured in basic mode with reportUnknownMemberType disabled

## Architecture

The agent initialization flow:

1. **CLI Entry**: `agent/__init__.py` - Main entry point that parses commands (start, dev, chat, simulate, replay)
2. **Agent Setup**: `agent/entrypoint.py` - Sets up LiveKit room, loads AI components, creates CallController
3. **Call Management**: `agent/call_controller.py` - Manages voice conversations using AgentManager
4. **Agent Stack**: `agent/agent_manager.py` - Manages transitions between different agent types

Key components:
- **Agent Types** (`agent/agents/`): Different conversation handlers (question, reschedule, transfer, etc.)
- **Services** (`agent/services/`): External integrations with LiveKit, Purplefish API, analytics
- **Schemas** (`agent/schemas/`): Data models for profiles, jobs, scripts, and user data
- **Script Nodes**: Define conversation flow, converted to agents at runtime

Key patterns:
- All code is async (asyncio)
- Service interfaces separate external dependencies
- Agent stack allows dynamic conversation state changes
- Extensive Pydantic usage for data validation

## Testing

Tests use pytest with async support. The codebase includes:
- Unit tests for individual components (run with `make test`)
- Simulation tests for end-to-end agent conversations (run with `make run-simulation`)
- Integration tests for agent behaviors
- Simulation tools for testing without real calls

When writing tests:
- Use `pytest.mark.asyncio` for async tests
- Mock external services via service interfaces
- Test files should mirror source structure
- Unit tests and simulation tests are separated for faster CI/CD
- Simulation tests include retry logic (3 attempts) for reliability
- Simulation tests run automatically on `git push` (bypass with `git push --no-verify`)

## Environment Configuration

The project uses 1Password CLI for secrets management. Environment files are in `envs/`:
- Development uses `envs/development.env`
- All commands automatically load appropriate env via `op run`
- Never commit secrets - use 1Password references

## Key Dependencies

- LiveKit SDK and plugins for WebRTC
- Deepgram for STT
- OpenAI (Azure) for LLM capabilities
- Datadog for monitoring
- uv for dependency management
- ty and pyright for type checking (dual system for speed and accuracy)

## Claude's Notes and Guidance

- If after trying something a few times you're stuck, please ask for clarification or help! I'm here for you claude <3

## Versioning and Release Management

The project uses Semantic Versioning with python-semantic-release. When creating releases:

### Commit Message Standards
Always use Conventional commit convention for clear version bumping:
- `feat:` for new features (minor version)
- `fix:` for bug fixes (patch version)
- `feat!:` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` for breaking changes (major version)

### Creating a Release
```bash
# Check what version would be created
uv run semantic-release version --print

# Create release (updates version, creates tag, updates CHANGELOG)
uv run semantic-release version

# Push changes and tags
git push --follow-tags origin main
```

## Voice Agent v4 Architecture (Added August 2025)

The latest commit introduces Voice Agent v4, a new modular architecture that replaces the previous agent system:

### New Components
- **voice_agent/**: New module for v4 implementation
  - `manager.py`: Core agent manager handling conversation state
  - `task_agent/`: Specialized agents (greeter, data_collection, information, closer)
  - `schemas/`: Data models for tasks, orchestration, and configuration
  - `utils/`: Utilities for orchestration, context management, and tool creation

### Key Changes from Previous Version
- Moved from monolithic agent to task-based architecture
- JSON script-driven conversation flow (`examples/it_support_call_script.json`)
- Dynamic tool generation based on script requirements
- Improved data point collection and validation
- Cleaner separation between conversation phases

### CLI Testing
- New CLI script at `scripts/cli.py` for testing v4 functionality
- Support for loading and executing call scripts
- Enhanced conversation context tracking
- Run with uv and 1Password: `op run --env-file=".voice_agent.env.example" -- uv run voice_agent_local_dev --call-script-path examples/it_support_call_script.json`

# Purplefish Agent

[![Test](https://github.com/purplefish-ai/agent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/purplefish-ai/agent/actions/workflows/test.yml)

This is our livekit based phone agent.

## Development

### Setup

1. Install the 1Password CLI: https://developer.1password.com/docs/cli/get-started/
2. Install uv: `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`
3. Install dependencies: `uv sync`
4. Install git hooks:
   ```bash
   # Install pre-commit hooks (runs on commit)
   pre-commit install

   # Install pre-push hooks (runs simulation tests on push)
   pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push

   # Or install both at once
   pre-commit install && pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push
   ```
5. Create local dev keys in Livekit
   1. Login to livekit, enter the `Local Dev <Your Name>` project (Martin will create this for you)
   2. go into Settings > Keys
   3. Create 1 new API Key
   4. Update the .env file to set the new API keys and Secrets. For local dev, we can use the same API key for all of these secrets.
      1. Set the API key to the values LIVEKIT_API_KEY_INBOUND, LIVEKIT_API_KEY_OUTBOUND
      2. Set the secret key to the values LIVEKIT_API_SECRET_INBOUND, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET_OUTBOUND
      3. Set the Websocket URL to the values LIVEKIT_URL_INBOUND, LIVEKIT_URL_OUTBOUND
6. Download the model files for livekit `make download-files`
7. Run the agent: `make dev`

## Testing the agent locally using the livekit playground
1. Find the profile you wish to test and copy the profile id
2. Paste the profile id into the default value for the `PLAYGROUND_PROFILE_ID` env var in `env.ts` on the *MONOREPO* (not in the agent repo)
3. Connect to the livekit agent playground by visiting this URL: https://agents-playground.livekit.io/
4. Select your local dev env
5. This will launch a new interview locally.

## Testing Tools

### Simulation Mode
Simulation mode allows you to run automated conversations between the agent and an AI-powered candidate using real job IDs.

**Usage:**
```bash
# Basic simulation
make simulate <job_id>

# With custom parameters
make simulate <job_id> max_turns=30
make simulate <job_id> instructions="You are an experienced candidate"
```

The simulation will:
- Fetch real job and profile data from your development server
- Run an automated conversation with an AI candidate (GPT-4)
- Display color-coded conversation transcript
- Provide evaluation of interview completion

### Interactive Chat Mode
Chat mode lets you interact directly with the agent as a candidate through text input.

**Usage:**
```bash
# Start interactive chat
make chat <job_id>
```

Features:
- Real-time text interaction with the agent
- You play the role of the candidate
- No turn limits - chat as long as you want
- Type 'exit', 'quit', 'bye', or 'goodbye' to end
- Color-coded output (your messages in green, agent in cyan)

Both modes create a room name in format `demo:{job_id}_{unique_id}` and use the real job data from your system.

## Debugging
If you need to run the agent through your IDE so that you can debug, here's how to do it
- Entrypoint should be the `agent` script. The agent script will be in your uv virtual environment at `.venv/bin/agent`
- Run the script with the param `start`
- You might need to configure your IDE to write secrets to a file before you launch. Here's an example command you can use for that: `inject -f -i ./envs/.env -o ./envs/local`

## Running lints and checks locally

### Pre-commit hooks
After making changes locally, you can manually run the hooks:
```bash
# Run all pre-commit hooks on all files
pre-commit run --all-files

# Run specific hook
pre-commit run ty --all-files
pre-commit run pyright --all-files
pre-commit run ruff-check --all-files

# Type checking - dual system for speed and accuracy
make ty-check     # Fast (10-20x faster), Rust-based, pre-alpha
make pyright      # Comprehensive, mature, production-ready
# Note: Both type checkers run in make check
```

### Pre-push hooks
To manually run pre-push checks:
```bash
# Run simulation tests (same as what happens on git push)
make run-simulation

# Or run pre-push hooks manually
pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push
```

This will let you catch lint issues and test failures before committing/pushing.

## Running the LiveKit CLI

We have a wrapper around the LiveKit CLI that respects the .env file.

First, install the LiveKit CLI with `brew install livekit-cli`

Run the LiveKit CLI with `uv run livekit <args...>`

## Testing

The project separates unit tests from simulation tests for better organization and faster CI/CD.

### Unit Tests

To run unit tests (excluding simulation tests):
```bash
# Run all unit tests in parallel
make test

# Run a specific test file or test
make test path=tests/unit/test_example.py
make test path=tests/unit/test_example.py::test_specific_function
```

Unit tests are run in parallel using pytest-xdist for faster execution and automatically exclude any simulation test directories.

### Simulation Tests

To run simulation tests (integration tests that simulate full conversations):
```bash
# Run all simulation tests
make run-simulation
```

Simulation tests:
- Run with retry logic (3 attempts with 1 second delay)
- Stop on first failure for easier debugging
- Test end-to-end agent behavior with simulated conversations
- **Note**: Simulation tests run automatically during `git push` via pre-push hook. To bypass this check, use `git push --no-verify`

### Code Coverage

We use pytest-cov to track code coverage. Coverage reports are automatically generated in CI/CD for all PRs.

**Running tests with coverage locally:**
```bash
# Run all tests with coverage
make test-cov

# Run specific test with coverage
make test-cov path=tests/unit/test_example.py

# Check coverage summary
uv run python scripts/check_coverage.py
```

**Coverage outputs:**
- **Terminal**: Coverage summary shown after tests complete
- **HTML Report**: Open `htmlcov/index.html` in your browser for detailed line-by-line coverage
- **XML Report**: `coverage.xml` for CI/CD integration

**Coverage in Pull Requests:**
- Coverage reports are automatically posted as PR comments (free, no external service required)
- Lines missing coverage are annotated in the PR diff
- Visual indicators: 🟢 85%+ | 🟡 70-84% | 🔴 <70%
- Coverage summary available in GitHub Actions job summary
- HTML coverage reports uploaded as artifacts for detailed analysis

**Current coverage targets:**
- Overall project: 70% minimum (aiming for 80%+)
- New code in PRs: 80% minimum

To get a more end-to-end-test, run purplefish-ai/app with inngest (`npm run inngest`). After the call, from the app
folder, run `npm run send-end-of-room-event` to trigger all of the end of room logic, including sending emails and SMS.

## Voice Agent v4

Voice Agent v4 introduces a new architecture with modular task-based agents. The foundation includes:
- **Task Orchestrator**: Manages conversation flow through defined tasks
- **Specialized Agents**: Greeter, DataCollection, Information, and Closer agents for different conversation phases
- **Dynamic Tool Factory**: Creates conversation tools based on script configuration
- **Conversation Context**: Maintains state and data points throughout the call
- **Script-Driven Architecture**: JSON-based call scripts define agent behavior and conversation flow

### Running Voice Agent v4 Locally

To test the new Voice Agent v4 with the local development command:

```bash
# Run with 1Password for environment variables and uv
op run --env-file=".voice_agent.env.example" -- uv run voice_agent_local_dev --call-script-path examples/it_support_call_script.json
```

For all local_dev options run
```bash
op run --env-file=".voice_agent.env.example" -- uv run voice_agent_local_dev --help
```

This command:
- Uses 1Password CLI to load environment variables from `.voice_agent.env.example`
- Runs the voice agent v4 local development mode
- Loads the example IT support call script for testing

## Docker Build and Run Guide

This guide explains how to build and run the Purplefish AI voice agent Docker image locally.

### Prerequisites

- Docker installed on your system
- 1Password CLI configured (for production deployment)
- Environment variables configured

### Building the Docker Image

Build the Docker image with:

```bash
docker build -t purplefish-agent:latest .
```

For a specific Python version:

```bash
docker build --build-arg PYTHON_VERSION=3.11 -t purplefish-agent:latest .
```

### Running the Docker Container

#### Development Mode (Local Testing)

For local development without 1Password integration, run with environment variables. See `envs/production.env` for the required variables:

```bash
# Set environment to bypass 1Password injection
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  -e VARIABLE_NAME="value" \
  # ... add all variables from envs/production.env ... \
  # can also pass in --env-file ./.env \
  purplefish-agent:latest
```

#### Production Mode (with 1Password)

For production deployment with 1Password service account:

```bash
docker run -it --rm \
  -e OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN="your-1password-service-account-token" \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Production \
  purplefish-agent:latest
```

#### Docker Command

By default, the container runs with `agent start` command

To run a different command (clarify in pyproject.toml project.scripts)

```bash
# Generate development room token
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  # ... environment variables from envs/production.env ... \
  purplefish-agent:latest voice_agent_local_dev --call-script-path "..." --no-simulate-room

# Generate development room token
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  # ... environment variables from envs/production.env ... \
  purplefish-agent:latest generate_dev_room_token

# download livekit plugin
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  # ... environment variables from envs/production.env ... \
  purplefish-agent:latest download_livekit_plugin_model
```

### Environment Variables

The container requires environment variables defined in `envs/production.env`. When running locally without 1Password:

- Set `AGENT_ENV=Development` to bypass 1Password injection
- Provide actual values for all variables listed in `envs/production.env`

For production with 1Password:
- Set `AGENT_ENV=Production`
- Provide `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` for 1Password service account access

### How It Works

1. The Dockerfile creates a lightweight Python 3.11 image
2. Installs system dependencies and required tools (1Password CLI, uv)
3. Creates a non-root user for security
4. Installs Python dependencies and downloads LiveKit plugin models
5. Uses `docker_entrypoint.sh` to handle environment setup:
   - In Production mode: Injects secrets from 1Password
   - In other modes: Uses passed environment variables
6. Runs the agent with DataDog tracing enabled

### Troubleshooting

- **Missing environment variables**: Ensure all required variables are set when not using 1Password
- **1Password errors**: Verify your service account token is valid and has access to required secrets
- **Model download issues**: The container pre-downloads LiveKit plugin models during build
- **Permission errors**: The container runs as non-root user `appuser` for security

## Versioning and Releases

This project uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) and [python-semantic-release](https://python-semantic-release.readthedocs.io/) for version management.

### Commit Message Convention
We follow the [Conventional Commits specification](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):

- `feat:` New feature (minor version bump)
- `fix:` Bug fix (patch version bump)
- `docs:` Documentation changes (no version bump)
- `style:` Code style changes (no version bump)
- `refactor:` Code refactoring (no version bump)
- `perf:` Performance improvements (patch version bump)
- `test:` Test changes (no version bump)
- `chore:` Build process or auxiliary tool changes (no version bump)
- `BREAKING CHANGE:` or `!` after type (major version bump)

Examples:
```
feat: add voice agent v4 support
fix: resolve timeout issue in call controller
feat!: redesign agent manager API
```

### Manual Release Process

To create a new release:

```bash
# Check what version will be released (dry run)
uv run semantic-release version --print

# Create a new version (updates version in pyproject.toml, creates git tag, updates CHANGELOG.md)
uv run semantic-release version

# Push the changes and tags to trigger GitHub release
git push --follow-tags origin main

# Optionally publish to GitHub releases
uv run semantic-release publish
```

The release process will:
1. Analyze commits since last release
2. Determine version bump based on commit types
3. Update version in `pyproject.toml`
4. Generate/update `CHANGELOG.md`
5. Create git tag with version
6. Create GitHub release with changelog
